how_this_works: Each hypothesis is falsifiable: it carries predictions with metrics and thresholds.
Signals (signal.* observations in Hydra) are assigned to a hypothesis parent.
Ideas declare hypothesis_parents; admission prefers aligned ideas and applies H1 as a hard filter via chatgpt_limits.json.
Periodically we compare each hypothesis' tracked series against its predictions -> status becomes playing_out / not_playing_out -> resources shift to playing hypotheses.

hypotheses.statement: Anything ChatGPT can do well is doomed as a separate product. Therefore maintain a list of things ChatGPT cannot do well; that list shrinks the problem space of what we build.

filter.mechanism: registry/chatgpt_limits.json capability classes; an idea whose core job falls outside every listed class is rejected at admission

predictions.claim: wrapper products whose core job is one good chat prompt plateau near zero recurring usage

hypotheses.statement: Build convenient tools for the agentic future such that it makes sense for agents to call them vs doing the work themselves — the tool must save tokens/time/effort or provide something chat lacks (live data, deterministic verification, persistence, side effects).

filter.mechanism: rubric features verifiability + data_access + low_integration_cost reward agent-convenience; WorkOrder spec must state the token-saving or capability delta

predictions.claim: agent-facing endpoints (machine-discoverable, typed, cheap) get disproportionate usage vs human-only pages
predictions.metric: ratio api.calls : web visits per product

predictions.claim: products exposing MCP tools see agent-origin traffic share grow over time

hypotheses.statement: Subscription models are dead — most people treat them like one-off purchases anyway. Given near-free compute, remake subscription SaaS from scratch and offer it free to maximize usage (usage is the asset: data, distribution, agent-dependency).

filter.mechanism: no auth/billing/subscription scaffolding in MVPs (already a Lane-A rule); incumbent_price signals justify unbundles; free serving cost must be ~0

predictions.claim: free-tier unbundles of paid incumbents reach usage parity with paid originals faster than paid clones would
incumbent prices in our niches rise while our free equivalents gain usage (arbitrage window open)
predictions.metric: signal.incumbent_price_min slope > 0 AND platform usage slope > 0

hypotheses.statement: Within 90 days, agent-commerce infrastructure increasingly gates payment release on machine-verifiable proof of execution (signed receipts/attestations), observable as a rising share of x402-discoverable commerce resources advertising receipt/proof/escrow semantics.
hypotheses.mechanism: Payment networks and marketplaces carry fraud/dispute risk they cannot price when an agent's claim of 'task done' is unverifiable. Escrow-by-proof converts disputes (expensive, human-adjudicated) into signature checks (cheap, deterministic), so rational platforms adopt proof-gating before regulators or chargeback economics force them to. Standards bodies (IETF SCITT, FIDO) standardize last, confirming buyer-side demand already exists.

This is not another protocol: it is a market-structure claim that proof-gating becomes a settlement prerequisite, which predicts DEMAND for those protocol products and is falsifiable independently of whether we build any of them.

hypotheses.statement: Reputation systems grounded in verifiable interaction receipts will displace self-reported reputation in agent ecosystems within two quarters, visible as accelerating traction of receipt-grounding reference implementations while ungrounded reputation registries stall.
hypotheses.mechanism: Self-reported reputation is Sybil-cheap: an empirical ERC-8004 study found records rarely grounded in verifiable interactions and heavily manipulated. When trust signals are cheap to fake, buyers discount them to zero and rationally pay for grounded alternatives — the same substitution for which Truepic already extracts enterprise revenue in insurance/lending/warranties. Signed receipts (SCITT-style) make grounding nearly free at the margin, collapsing the cost differential that kept self-reported reputation dominant.

hypotheses.novelty_note: existing_ideas has reputation PRODUCTS (vent_capability_reputation, vent_1786993091_reputation, vent_1786993093_reputation, vent_work_receipt___reput). Those propose building a grounded-reputation service; this hypothesis predicts the ADOPTION CURVE and displacement direction, so it can PASS even if none of our products ship, and its failure would demote the whole reputation-product family.

hypotheses.statement: Rentable-human marketplaces (agents purchasing human actions) show sustained supply growth, and their binding constraint migrates from sourcing supply to machine-verifiable completion of human tasks — making machine-readable human-work receipts the scarce commodity, not the marketplace itself.
hypotheses.mechanism: Agents cannot produce CAPTCHA passes, wet signatures, physical presence, or jurisdictionally-bound identifications; marketplaces supplying these emerged organically and reached scale fast (RentAHuman reports 784k+ listed humans across 100+ countries with REST/MCP access), which only happens under pre-existing demand. As supply deepens, competition compresses marketplace margins toward zero (listing is undifferentiated), but acceptance automation does not commoditize: an agent that cannot verify a human actually performed the task either overpays for fraud or drowns in disputes — so value migrates to the verifiable-completion layer, exactly the proof-before-payment pattern MeatLayer already runs for physical jobs.

hypotheses.novelty_note: existing_ideas includes vent_human_escalation_api, vent_realityrouter, and human-inference verification protocols (VENT_1786992636_*). All are build proposals for one side of the market. This hypothesis makes a claim ABOUT the market — liquidity keeps growing while the bottleneck migrates to verification — which tells us whether to build the escalation API at all or skip straight to the receipt layer.

hypotheses.statement: Episodic-use subscription SaaS is attackable with free/one-shot agent-and-human-optimized unbundles: NO ACCOUNT, NO SUBSCRIPTION — do the job, leave. Value migrates from subscriptions to micropayments/usage; we arbitrage by finding incumbents whose pricing insults their usage frequency, recreating core features, and taking usage share.

filter.mechanism: ideas must name an incumbent with visible recurring pricing AND episodic usage (<=4x/year per typical user); UnbundleScore components recorded

predictions.claim: incumbents in our niches raise prices or add tier walls over 6 months while our free alternatives accumulate usage
